transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... it's about my eating. After I do it, I just sit there looking at all the empty containers and wrappers, and I feel completely disgusted with myself. I've always tried to be a steady, in-control kind of man, and... I just feel like I'm not that guy anymore when this happens. I need to get a handle on it.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you do anything to try to counteract it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or fasting?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't throw up or take anything like laxatives. And I'm definitely not out there exercising for hours or starving myself afterward. I just... sit with it, really. I just feel bad about it, but I don't do anything to try and undo it.
During these episodes when you eat a lot, do you feel like you can't stop eating or that you've lost control over how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly how it is. Once I start... it feels like the same discipline I have out on the road just completely shuts off. It's a strange thing, because even while I’m sitting there telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down,' I just can't do it. My hand just keeps going back for more. I definitely lose control over it.
How often do these episodes of losing control and eating a lot happen? For example, is it happening multiple times a week, once a week, a few times a month, or less frequently than that?

Well, since I’ve been home dealing with a back injury, it’s been happening pretty often. I'd say it happens several nights most weeks. Honestly, I really can’t think of a single week in these past three months where I didn’t have at least one of those episodes.

You mentioned you don't make yourself vomit or use laxatives afterward. But I want to make sure I have the full picture—after these episodes, do you ever try to 'make up for it' in any way, like by restricting what you eat the next day or doing intense exercise to burn it off?

No, I really don't. Like I said, I'm laid up with this back injury, so intense exercise is completely out of the question anyway. And as for restricting what I eat the next day... no, I don't do that either. I just eat my normal meals the next day. I don't try to make up for it or undo it at all.

These episodes where you lose control and eat a lot—how much do they bother you or interfere with your life? For example, do they affect your mood, your relationships, or how you feel about yourself in a significant way?

It bothers me a lot, honestly. It really takes a toll on how I view myself. It's actually getting to the point where... well, I’m supposed to be mentoring some of the newer drivers from the company, but lately I’ve started avoiding their check-in calls. I just feel so ashamed of what's going on, and I really don’t want anyone hearing how far off my routine I’ve gotten. So yeah, it's definitely interfering with things.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight or how your clothes fit since these eating episodes started happening more frequently over the past three months?

I haven't really weighed myself lately, to be honest. And since I've been stuck at home with this back injury, I'm mostly just wearing sweatpants and loose shirts anyway. So... I can't really say for sure if my regular work clothes are fitting differently, or if my weight has actually changed. I just haven't been keeping track of it.

I understand you haven't been weighing yourself, but have you noticed that your body looks or feels different to you—like your stomach, face, or how your body feels overall—compared to before these eating episodes started three months ago?

Not really, no. Like I said, I'm mostly just sitting around in sweats because of my back, so I haven't been paying much attention to how I look in the mirror. I feel sluggish, sure, but I don't know if I actually look different. I just haven't noticed.

When you say these episodes happen 'several nights most weeks,' can you give me a more specific number? On average over the past three months, how many times per week would you say you have one of these episodes where you lose control and eat a lot?

Well, since I've been stuck at home with this back injury, it's... it's been happening a lot. I'd say several nights most weeks. Honestly, I can't think of a single week in these past three months where I didn't have at least one of those episodes. If I had to put a number on it... probably four or five times a week, on average.
